name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP power cut 8 Nov; worker killed 9 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost off-site power on 8 Nov and a worker was killed by a drone on 9 Nov; IAEA warns of winter grid risk
state: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power for more than 12 hours on 8 Nov after a 330kV line was damaged, the 27th such loss of the conflict, and on 15 Nov IAEA Director General Grossi warned that the state of Ukraine's grid poses serious nuclear safety risks that may grow in winter (APA). On 9 Nov a plant worker was killed in a drone attack, the second since 29 Oct, and the IAEA said attacks on nuclear workers must cease (United24). Searches on 18 Nov found no damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the UK. For official information on nuclear safety in Ukraine, follow IAEA updates; anyone travelling to the region should check FCDO travel advice for Ukraine.
rubric_hit: Watch: ZNPP lost all off-site power on 8 Nov and IAEA reports deteriorating grid safety; no safety-system damage (Alert line)

sources.title: APA — Grossi: nuclear safety risks at Zaporizhzhia NPP may increase in winter
United24 Media — Drone kills Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker, second in under two weeks

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
